newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crudes steady late, demand moderate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crudes steady late, demand moderate.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes held steady in thin dealings Wednesday propped by moderate refiner demand and a still bullish outlook for heating oil.
Grade differentials recovered some ground after Tuesday's drop, but aggressive buying was not seen.
"We've been buying fob barrels lately only because there just aren't many light foreign cargoes on offer," a Midwest refinery trader said, noting support for Louisiana crudes.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.05-15 a barrel, down 35 cents from Tuesday, after the market flirted with intraday lows at $24.71 and highs at $25.70.
Nov/Dec WTI stayed mostly locked in a range around 32-35 cts, which kept WTI/Cushing Posting Plus steady at postings plus $2.07-2.12 a barrel. Trade was seen at $2.12.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at 58 cts over WTI/Cushing, some four to six cts higher than Tuesday.
One parcel for December was reported done at 70 cents premium to WTI, which underlined nervousness about a potential shortage of sweet crude supplies due to expensive imports.
WTI/Midland traded at 6 and 7 cents premium before succumbing to selling pressures, drifting to 3/4 cents, but not likely to spiral into negative territory.
Midwest crude stocks at 65 million barrels continued to render support amid relatively expensive imports.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was steady at 45 cts premium.
Sour grades steadied with minimal interest seen due to more ample regional alternatives.
West Texas Sour/Midland moved at WTI minus $1.38 a barrel, around the low end of Tuesday's range. And Eugene Island was valued at minus $1.10, five cents weaker, with no trade seen.
